title: Free one-vertex completions of a nonfree product chain
statement: Use the finite totally ordered sets $[r]=\{0<\cdots<r\}$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $m\geq0$ and $n\geq1$ be integers and let $P=\{0,\ldots,m\}\times\{0,\ldots,n\}$ have the coordinatewise order. A strict chain means a finite nonempty sequence of distinct elements of $P$ increasing in this order. Call a chain free if both coordinate projections are surjective and it contains $(b,0)$ and $(b,1)$ for some $b\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$. Let $\tau$ be a strict chain whose first coordinates contain every element of $\{0,\ldots,m\}$, whose second coordinates contain $1,\ldots,n$, and which contains no pair $(b,0),(b,1)$. Let $(p,1)$ be its first vertex with second coordinate $1$. The initial segment of $\tau$ ending at that vertex is exactly $(0,0)<\cdots<(p-1,0)<(p,1)$, interpreted as just $(0,1)$ when $p=0$. The free strict chains obtained from $\tau$ by inserting exactly one vertex are precisely the chain obtained by inserting $(p,0)$ immediately before $(p,1)$ and, when $p>0$, the chain obtained by inserting $(p-1,1)$ immediately after $(p-1,0)$. The former has its unique vertical $0$-to-$1$ pair in positions $p,p+1$, and the latter in positions $p-1,p$, with positions numbered from zero.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 4.4.4.7, proof: exhaustion paragraph and final paragraph (nonfree missing face and the only other free enlargement); explicit finite-poset formulation. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $(p,1)$ be the first vertex of $\tau$ whose second coordinate is $1$. For every $a<p$, surjectivity of the first projection supplies a vertex with first coordinate $a$. Such a vertex must occur before $(p,1)$, so its second coordinate is at most $1$; by minimality of $(p,1)$ it is $0$. Strict increase in the product order then forces these vertices, in order, to be $(0,0),(1,0),\ldots,(p-1,0)$. The vertex $(p,0)$ cannot occur, because together with $(p,1)$ it would violate the hypothesis that $\tau$ has no vertical $0$-to-$1$ pair. Thus the asserted initial segment is exactly the one displayed (and for $p=0$ it is just $(0,1)$).

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, exhaustion paragraph: choose the first vertex with second coordinate 1 and identify the initial chain.

proof.text: Suppose that inserting one vertex $x$ into $\tau$ gives a free chain $\tau'$. By definition $\tau'$ contains a pair $(b,0),(b,1)$. Since $\tau$ contains no such pair and $\tau'$ differs from $\tau$ only by $x$, the vertex $x$ is one of the two vertices of this pair. If $x=(b,0)$, then $(b,1)$ is already in $\tau$; if $x=(b,1)$, then $(b,0)$ is already in $\tau$. (The surjectivity requirements give no further constraint on $x$: $\tau$ already has every first coordinate and every second coordinate $1,\ldots,n$, and the second coordinate $0$ is supplied by the pair.)

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, missing-face analysis: the inserted vertex must complete a vertical pair.

proof.text: In the case $x=(b,0)$, the required partner $(b,1)$ lies in $\tau$. Since $(p,1)$ is its first level-$1$ vertex, monotonicity gives $b\geq p$. If $b>p$, then $(b,0)$ is incomparable with the existing $(p,1)$: the first coordinate is larger but the second coordinate is smaller. Hence $b=p$. Step 1 shows that $(p,0)$ is absent, and that its only possible position is immediately before $(p,1)$, after $(p-1,0)$ when $p>0$. This gives the first asserted insertion.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, exhaustion paragraph: insert $(p,0)$ immediately before $(p,1)$.

proof.text: In the case $x=(b,1)$, the required partner $(b,0)$ lies in $\tau$. Every level-$0$ vertex precedes $(p,1)$, so step 1 gives $0\leq b<p$. If $b<p-1$, then the existing vertex $(b+1,0)$ is incomparable with $(b,1)$: its first coordinate is larger and its second coordinate is smaller. Thus $b=p-1$ and $p>0$. Step 1 shows that $(p-1,1)$ is absent, and its position is forced to be immediately after $(p-1,0)$ and immediately before $(p,1)$. This is the second asserted insertion; for $p=0$ the level-$0$ partner does not exist, so this case is impossible.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, final paragraph: the only other free enlargement inserts $(p-1,1)$ and has index $p-1$.

proof.text: Conversely, each displayed insertion is order-preserving and strict: $(p-1,0)<(p,0)<(p,1)$ (the first inequality only when $p>0$) in the first case, while $(p-1,0)<(p-1,1)<(p,1)$ in the second. The first projection stays surjective because $\tau$'s was. The second projection contains $1,\ldots,n$ from $\tau$ and $0$ from the inserted pair; this matters when $p=0$, where $\tau$ has no vertex of second coordinate $0$ by step 1. Two vertices $(b,0),(b,1)$ of a chain are adjacent, since a vertex between them would have to equal one of them. The inserted vertical pair is the unique one: any such pair either lies in $\tau$, which has none, or contains the inserted vertex, whose only partner is the displayed one. By step 1 the vertices before the pair are $(0,0),\ldots,(p-1,0)$, so the pair occupies positions $p,p+1$ in the first chain and $p-1,p$ in the second, counting from zero. This proves the stated classification and position claims.

lean.statement: theorem nonfreeChain_completions (m n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (τ : List (Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1))) (hchain : τ.Pairwise (fun x y ↦ x.1 ≤ y.1 ∧ x.2 ≤ y.2 ∧ x ≠ y)) (hfst : ∀ a : Fin (m + 1), ∃ x ∈ τ, x.1 = a) (hsnd : ∀ c : Fin (n + 1), 1 ≤ c.val → ∃ x ∈ τ, x.2 = c) (hnopair : ∀ b : Fin (m + 1), ¬ ((b, 0) ∈ τ ∧ (b, 1) ∈ τ)) (p : Fin (m + 1)) (k : ℕ) (hfirst : τ[k]? = some (p, 1)) (hbefore : ∀ j < k, ∀ x, τ[j]? = some x → x.2.val ≠ 1) : k = p.val ∧ (τ.take (k + 1)).map (fun x ↦ (x.1.val, x.2.val)) = (List.range p.val).map (fun a ↦ (a, 0)) ++ [(p.val, 1)] ∧ (∀ σ : List (Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)), (IsFreePrismChain σ ∧ ∃ (i : ℕ) (x : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (n + 1)), i ≤ τ.length ∧ x ∉ τ ∧ σ = τ.insertIdx i x) ↔ σ = τ.insertIdx p.val (p, 0) ∨ ∃ b : Fin (m + 1), b.val + 1 = p.val ∧ σ = τ.insertIdx p.val (b, 1)) ∧ (τ.insertIdx p.val (p, 0))[p.val]? = some (p, 0) ∧ (τ.insertIdx p.val (p, 0))[p.val + 1]? = some (p, 1) ∧ (∀ b : Fin (m + 1), ((b, 0) ∈ τ.insertIdx p.val (p, 0) ∧ (b, 1) ∈ τ.insertIdx p.val (p, 0)) ↔ b = p) ∧ (∀ b : Fin (m + 1), b.val + 1 = p.val → (τ.insertIdx p.val (b, 1))[b.val]? = some (b, 0) ∧ (τ.insertIdx p.val (b, 1))[p.val]? = some (b, 1) ∧ ∀ a : Fin (m + 1), ((a, 0) ∈ τ.insertIdx p.val (b, 1) ∧ (a, 1) ∈ τ.insertIdx p.val (b, 1)) ↔ a = b)
